title: Russian Missiles Kill 10, Injure 17 in Pechenihy, Kharkiv Oblast
detail: Two Russian Banderol cruise missiles struck the village of Pechenihy in Kharkiv Oblast at 08:40, hitting a post office and shops at a crossroads ringed by homes just as residents were heading to work, according to settlement head Oleksandr Husarov. At least 10 people were killed and 17 injured; a cafe and at least 7 vehicles were set ablaze, 10 private homes and a store were damaged across roughly 400 square meters. President Zelensky said Russia "brutally struck a crowded crossroads" and vowed a response, while Acting Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha accused Moscow of continuing "to drag out the war instead of accepting Ukraine's realistic ceasefire proposals."

title: Russian Tornado-S Rocket Strike on Izium Injures Five, Including Child
detail: Russian forces struck Izium in Kharkiv Oblast at around 04:05 with a 300mm Tornado-S multiple-launch rocket system, injuring 5 people including a 9-year-old boy who suffered shrapnel wounds from broken glass and his 18-year-old brother who sustained a contusion. Three other adults suffered acute stress reactions. Twenty private homes were damaged. The Izium District Prosecutor's Office opened a war-crimes investigation under Article 438 of Ukraine's Criminal Code.

title: Ukraine Launches 620-Drone Assault on Moscow for Second Consecutive Night
detail: Ukraine launched more than 620 drones at Moscow and the surrounding region overnight into August 18 — its largest such attack in years and a second consecutive night of large-scale aerial retaliation. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said 180-197 drones were shot down over Moscow Oblast. At least 3 people, including a 10-year-old girl in Ramensky who suffered shrapnel injuries when a drone crashed into a private home, were injured; roughly 5,000 residents lost power. A Wildberries warehouse, a residential building in Pavlovsky Posad, an aluminum plant, and the Globus shopping center in Kolomna were damaged. Vnukovo, Domodedovo, and Zhukovsky airports suspended flights.
